newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end mixed before weekend.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end mixed before weekend.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mixed in quiet trade ahead of the long Presidents Day holiday weekend.
U.S. debt futures closed early and the morning's slim stock index volume tapered off even more once those markets closed. Trading will be closed for the U.S. holiday on Monday.

March Standard and Poor's 500 futures reached a fresh record high overnight at 817.45 but remained below there during the day session, plagued by mild profit-taking amid thin trading pits, traders said.
Heading into the close, March S&P 500 volume on Chicago Mercantile Exchange price boards was estimated at 65,000 contracts. One trader said that estimate was overstated.
"I think people gave up heading into the weekend," he said, adding that long position holders were happy with their profits while shorts likely threw in the towel until Tuesday.

March S&Ps slipped to a session low of 810.25 after debt futures closed. Traders called 810.00 good support, and kept bullish upside targets at 820.00 to 825.00. They said a bullish momentum was intact, especially after this week's run to new highs.

Strong Treasury bonds underpinned S&Ps earlier, with soft producer price data helping the bullish T-bond tone. January producer prices fell 0.3 percent overall, with the rate excluding volatile food and energy sectors unchanged. Overall trade estimates had been for a rise of 0.3 percent and a 0.2 percent core rate gain.
Industrial production for January was unchanged and December revised to up 0.5 percent. Capacity use was pegged at 83.3 percent compared with 83.5 percent in December.

At the end of pit trading, March S&Ps were down 1.95 points to 812.20, Value Lines were 0.95 higher at 718.10, NYSE Composites were 0.05 lower at 425.45, Nikkeis were 30 higher at 18,770, Midcap 400s were up 0.15 at 269.95 and Nasdaq 100s were off 4.95 at 903.80.
